rationale: Both cold candidate runs promoted streaming at 12 workers after two independently passing A/B/A comparisons; runtime ISA and two-confirmation gates remain unchanged.
Both cold and cached productive pairs improved. Fixed AVX2 controls were 0.36-0.82% slower; no build-effect correction was applied to the automatic gains.
All eight commands used automatic worker and kernel selection, a 24-worker ceiling and explicit 2 MiB HugeTLB. No fixed worker or kernel override.
All four restarts reused their own cold worker count. Candidate restarts began at 18 workers, and logs subsequently showed streaming-cache restoration during count exploration.

All 21 full-size reference transitions passed; resource lifecycle completed without swap or OOM. Under temporary memory limits workers parked; constrained restart retained the remembered count of 3 and recovered from 1 to 2 workers within the observed window. Recovery to 3 was not demonstrated.
Accept identity-scoped candidate eligibility, with normal runtime confirmation; do not force streaming at startup or extrapolate VM throughput to a full socket.
limitations: Two pairs per phase in one VM session; descriptive finite-window gains, not a population confidence interval or steady-state peak.
Physical memory channels and DIMM speed, package power and wall power unmeasured.
At 18/24-worker contexts, retaining the streaming incumbent after losing challengers is not a new two-cycle streaming promotion.
Measurements use the frozen recorded revisions, not a later integration build.
